data: Soviet Venus + Halley double mission — first interplanetary balloon, first Halley flyby

First spacecraft of the international Halley armada. Launched 1984-12-15 on a Proton-K / D-1 from Baikonur. The spacecraft, about 4900 kg in total, carried a ~1500 kg descent module that separated for Venus arrival 1985-06-11 — the lander touched down at 7.5°N, 177.8°E for 56 minutes of surface science, while a first-of-kind helium-filled balloon aerostat floated in the cloud deck at 54 km altitude for 46 hours tracking wind speeds + atmospheric structure across two thirds of the planet. The Vega-1 flyby bus then continued on its 9-month cruise to comet 1P/Halley, encountering the nucleus 1986-03-06 at 8889 km — the first Halley encounter of the armada, providing the targeting data ESA's Giotto used 8 days later for its much closer 596 km approach. Twin spacecraft Vega-2 launched 6 days later.
Sagdeev et al. (1986) — Vega + the Halley armada (Nature 321)
Soviet Venus + Halley's Comet double mission — Venera lander, first interplanetary balloon, then Halley flyby

First spacecraft of the international Halley armada. Launched 1984-12-15 on a Proton-K / D-1. The spacecraft, about 4900 kg in total, carried a ~1500 kg descent module that separated for Venus arrival 1985-06-11 — the lander touched down at 7.5°N, 177.8°E for 56 minutes of surface science, while a first-of-kind helium-filled balloon aerostat floated in the cloud deck at 54 km altitude for 46 hours tracking wind speeds and atmospheric structure. The flyby bus continued on its 9-month cruise and encountered comet 1P/Halley 1986-03-06 at 8889 km — the first Halley encounter of the armada, providing the targeting data ESA's Giotto used 8 days later for its much closer 596 km approach.
First-ever balloon aerostat deployed in another planet's atmosphere (Venus, 1985); first spacecraft to visit both a planet and a comet
